name: Sports coat / odd jacket

lead: A sport coat (also sports jacket or odd jacket) is a tailored jacket designed to be worn without matching trousers. It sits between a casual shirt and a suit in formality and comes in more colours, patterns and textures than most suit jackets.
For looks, a well-fitted jacket gives the shoulders and chest a defined line and creates a smarter silhouette than a plain shirt or knitwear.

paras: It is typically worn over a shirt or knit with chinos, jeans or odd trousers. Common cloths include tweed, flannel, corduroy, hopsack and linen, chosen by season and occasion.
No health concerns; the main practical issue is fit, because shoulders, sleeve length and jacket length are what make it look tailored.

chain: Layered, smarter outfit with ordinary trousers
angle.text: A tailored jacket adds structure at the shoulders and a defined waist line, which changes how the torso reads. Because it is not matched to trousers, it can be worn with jeans or chinos for a dressed-up look that stays casual.

lead: A sport coat, also called a sports jacket or odd jacket, is a smart-casual lounge jacket with flap pockets that is designed to be worn on its own rather than as part of a matching suit [1].

It began as clothing for country sports such as shooting and riding and was later adopted by spectators at outdoor events; the Norfolk jacket is the oldest form [1]. Because it is not tied to a trouser match, it can be paired with many different trousers, and it comes in a wider range of styles, colours and patterns than most suits [1].
Wool, and especially tweed such as Donegal, is the classic material, with corduroy, hopsack, flannel and linen also common [1].

paras: Wikipedia describes the sport coat as a lounge jacket meant to be worn alone, in contrast to a suit jacket sold with matching trousers [1]. A blazer is similar but usually solid-coloured or in wide vertical stripes, often with metal buttons and patch pockets, which links it to naval and boating dress; sport coats and most suit jackets lack patch pockets [1].
The garment grew out of country-sports attire, with later adoption by people attending outdoor events [1].
Style discussions treat jackets as an upgrade over casual tops because a tailored cut shapes the shoulders. No community material about this specific garment is available.
